about: These papers cut overthinking in reasoning models through chain-of-thought compression, adaptive token budgets, early stopping, parallel thinking and latent or implicit reasoning.

These papers compress language models through structured pruning, quantization and distillation and measure real inference speedups, while the cluster also mixes in assorted training, data selection and representation studies.
These papers compare language models with human sentence processing and test their syntactic, lexical and typological knowledge, with a mix of morphology, parsing and corpus work.

These papers evaluate and train models for clinical decision making over electronic health records, multi-turn medical consultations and diagnosis, with a focus on evidence use and rubric-based assessment.

These papers analyze why chain-of-thought reasoning fails, whether reasoning traces are faithful, and how to benchmark logical and causal reasoning, alongside work on overthinking and test-time compute.
These papers study whether models know what they know, covering verbal confidence calibration, belief stability, honesty, overconfidence and hallucination mechanisms.
These papers improve how RAG systems select, trust and cite retrieved evidence, covering knowledge conflicts, poisoning robustness, attribution and RAG evaluation.
These papers measure and close the gap between English and other languages through cross-lingual alignment, representation analysis, multilingual judges and multilingual training data.

topic: Cognitive Bias, Sycophancy and Moral Judgment
about: These papers probe language models with methods from psychology and social science, measuring sycophancy, cognitive and social biases, persuasion, moral reasoning and human-model behavioral gaps.
These papers benchmark and debug LLM agents on real-world planning, enterprise workflows and MCP tool use, and diagnose failures from agent execution trajectories.
These papers design and benchmark long-term memory systems for conversational and personalized agents, covering memory extraction, consolidation, hierarchical organization and retrieval.
These papers study how safety alignment and refusal work inside models, defend against jailbreaks and over-refusal, preserve safety during fine-tuning and benchmark content moderation.
These papers refine reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards and on-policy distillation for reasoning, tackling credit assignment, entropy collapse, advantage estimation and label-free rewards.
These papers diagnose where vision-language models fail, including language priors overriding perception, framing effects, false premises, miscalibrated confidence and unfaithful visual grounding.

These papers analyze and redesign sequence model architectures such as Transformers, linear attention, Mamba-style state-space models and hybrids, covering positional encoding, attention sinks and layer representations.

These papers test how reliable LLM judges are, exposing position, self-preference and rubric biases and proposing debiasing, calibration and measurement-theory fixes, alongside a few fairness auditing studies.
These papers train dense and generative retrievers and LLM rerankers, with a focus on reasoning-intensive and efficient text retrieval.
These papers design jailbreak and backdoor attacks on language and vision-language models and defend against them with detection probes, guardrails and alignment interventions.
These papers train and evaluate code models with unit-test generation, execution feedback, reward models and debugging to make generated code functionally correct.

topic: Speech Language Models and Voice Agents
about: These papers evaluate and build speech language models, spoken dialogue systems and voice agents, covering speech recognition, speech translation, TTS evaluation and multilingual speech benchmarks.

topic: Diffusion Language Models and Parallel Decoding
about: These papers build, scale and speed up masked and continuous diffusion language models, with new remasking, parallel decoding, length control and distillation strategies.
These papers train and evaluate agents that run long-horizon web search for deep research, using reinforcement learning, synthetic search environments and trajectory synthesis.

These papers train language agents for long-horizon interactive tasks using learned world models, experience reuse, context management and self-evolving policies in environments like ALFWorld and WebShop.
These papers improve reinforcement learning for long-horizon agents and reasoning with better credit assignment, rubric and process rewards, rollout budgeting and defenses against reward hacking.

topic: Mathematical Reasoning and Formal Theorem Proving
about: These papers improve and evaluate mathematical problem solving through verifiers, process reward models, distractor robustness, autoformalization and formal proof benchmarks.

topic: Speech Synthesis, Recognition and Audio Tokenizers
about: These papers build and adapt speech and audio models for text-to-speech, speech recognition, streaming speech translation and audio tokenization.
These papers adapt pretrained models to new domains through supervised fine-tuning, continual pre-training and parameter-efficient methods while limiting catastrophic forgetting of general skills.

topic: Visually Grounded Multimodal Reasoning with RL
about: These papers train vision-language models to reason while keeping attention on visual evidence, using reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards, latent visual thinking and visual self-correction.

topic: Role-Playing Agents and Emotional Support Dialogue
about: These papers train and evaluate role-playing characters, counseling and emotional support agents, and user simulators for multi-turn dialogue, with some general conversational assistant work.

These papers study dialects, writing systems and romanized or cross-script text in Arabic, Indic, African and other low-resource languages, alongside a mix of other language-specific resources and benchmarks.
These papers use language models for research ideation, scientific discovery, paper writing and verification, and study how AI changes citation behavior and scientific prose.
These papers study how language models translate, build translation benchmarks and metrics, and improve document-level and low-resource machine translation with reasoning and reinforcement learning.

topic: Knowledge Graph Reasoning and Link Prediction
about: These papers reason over knowledge graphs and text-attributed graphs, covering KGQA, temporal knowledge graph forecasting, link prediction and graph serialization for language models.
These papers benchmark and steer how language models understand and adapt to cultural norms, values and region-specific knowledge across many languages and societies.
These papers benchmark and improve video-language models on temporal reasoning, captioning, cross-video question answering and text-to-video generation quality.
These papers measure and trace gender, racial and occupational stereotypes inside language models and debias them, with a share of work on steering vectors and refusal directions more generally.
These papers build new evaluation benchmarks across domains and languages and question benchmark validity through contamination detection, compression and diagnostic analysis.
These papers design and debug multi-agent LLM systems, covering role and topology adaptation, message pruning, latent communication, failure attribution and robustness to faulty agents.

topic: Multimodal RAG and Visual Document Retrieval
about: These papers retrieve images and visually rich documents with multimodal embeddings and late interaction, and use them in multimodal retrieval-augmented generation for long-document question answering.
These papers shrink the key-value cache for long-context inference through token eviction, quantization, low-rank approximation and adaptive per-layer budgets.

These papers study how assistants ask clarifying questions, answer information-seeking and misconception-laden queries, and evaluate open QA, mixed with assorted conversation analytics and pragmatics work.

These papers examine modality bias, uncertainty and robustness in omni-modal and multimodal models, mixed with assorted work on incomplete multimodal learning, emotion recognition and multimodal data pipelines.

topic: Tool Use and Function Calling Agents
about: These papers train and evaluate agents that select, retrieve and call external tools and APIs, with synthetic tool-use data, policy optimization and large tool ecosystems.
These papers answer multi-hop questions by retrieving evidence over knowledge graphs, hypergraphs and document graphs, often with agentic or iterative retrieval.

topic: Agent Skill Libraries and Skill Evolution
about: These papers let agents distill, retrieve, revise and evolve reusable procedural skills from execution traces, a topic that is new in 2026.
These papers generate and evaluate visual artifacts such as webpages, SVG graphics, diagrams, slides and charts from code, and benchmark text-to-image generation and editing.

These papers improve model reasoning through self-evolution, reinforcement learning with guided exploration, latent reasoning and activation steering, alongside some work on calibration and abstention.
These papers analyze and transfer writing style for authorship attribution and personalized generation, and measure diversity and creativity in machine-written stories and poetry.

topic: Document Information Extraction and Enterprise QA
about: These papers extract structured information from corporate, financial and office documents and benchmark question answering over enterprise document collections, with some legal and biomedical extraction mixed in.
These papers detect and reduce hallucinations, mostly object hallucinations in vision-language models, using attention-head interventions, activation steering, decoding fixes and new benchmarks.
These papers adapt model responses to individual users through user profiles, memory selection, preference tracing, persona steering and personality or value alignment.
These papers verify claims against retrieved evidence, score the factuality of long-form generations and detect fake news, including robustness to conflicting or adversarial evidence.
These papers benchmark and guard tool-using agents against unsafe actions, prompt injection, malicious skills, privacy leaks and backdoors during multi-step execution.
These papers benchmark and train coding agents on repository-level tasks such as issue localization, program repair, code retrieval and refactoring.

topic: Entity Linking, Relation Extraction and Taxonomies
about: These papers link entities to knowledge bases, extract relations and named entities, and induce taxonomies, mixed with assorted work on topic modeling, embedding geometry and intent discovery.

topic: User Simulators and Human Behavior Simulation
about: These papers use language models to simulate users, personas and social behavior for evaluating agents and studying surveys and online discourse, and test how faithful these simulations are.
These papers study how humans and LLMs annotate data, covering annotator disagreement and label variation, noisy labels, annotation guidelines and cost-aware human-AI labeling pipelines.
These papers build LLM-based recommender systems that generate semantic item IDs, model user histories and preferences, and suggest queries in e-commerce search.
These papers help video language models answer questions about long and streaming videos through frame selection, evidence search and hierarchical multimodal memory.
These papers improve low-rank adaptation through rank allocation, initialization and multi-task packing, and use adapters to limit forgetting in continual and federated fine-tuning.

topic: Automated Peer Review and Essay Scoring
about: These papers generate, verify and audit scientific peer reviews with language models, alongside work on multi-trait essay scoring and deep research report evaluation.
These papers build and diagnose vision-language-action policies for robot manipulation, navigation and autonomous driving, including grounding, planning and paraphrase robustness.
These papers detect and attribute machine-generated text with zero-shot statistics, probes and trained detectors, and audit detector shortcuts, robustness and cross-lingual performance.

topic: Medical Question Answering and Medical VQA
about: These papers build and evaluate medical reasoning models for question answering and medical visual question answering, using reinforcement learning, multilingual medical data and evidence-grounded training.
These papers speed up language model inference with draft models, draft trees, retrieval-based drafting and smarter verification, plus related work on efficient sampling.
These papers apply language models and agents to molecular property prediction, molecular optimization, retrosynthesis, structure elucidation, protein design and drug discovery.
These papers evaluate and build models and agents for finance, covering financial reasoning benchmarks, retrieval, forecasting, trading, compliance and hallucination detection.

topic: Direct Preference Optimization and Personalized Alignment
about: These papers refine preference alignment with token-weighted and noise-robust DPO variants, preference data selection, multi-objective steering and personalized or pluralistic alignment.
These papers attack and defend tool-using agents against indirect prompt injection and build red-teaming methods and benchmarks for agent security.
These papers build benchmarks, retrieval systems and reasoning models for legal judgment prediction, legal case retrieval and legal question answering across jurisdictions.
These papers translate natural language into SQL with schema linking, chain-of-thought training, reinforcement learning and candidate selection, and build more realistic text-to-SQL benchmarks.

topic: Privacy Leakage, PII and Membership Inference
about: These papers measure and mitigate privacy risks through PII detection, text sanitization, re-identification audits, membership inference and contextual integrity in agents.
These papers improve multi-agent debate for reasoning through better moderation, memory and aggregation, and study persuasion, counterargument generation and competitive debating.
These papers compress model weights, activations and KV caches with post-training, mixed-precision, ternary and quantization-aware methods that handle outliers.

topic: Table Reasoning and Table Question Answering
about: These papers answer questions and reason over tables, including multi-table retrieval, SQL-guided decomposition, table graphs and multimodal table images.
These papers build benchmarks, simulators and frameworks for agents that operate mobile apps, desktops and web interfaces, testing long-horizon tasks, ambiguity handling and safety.

topic: Optimization Modeling and Evolutionary Algorithm Discovery
about: These papers use language models to formulate operations research and optimization problems and to evolve algorithms, code and designs through search-based self-improvement loops.

topic: Visual Token Pruning for Efficient VLMs
about: These papers cut inference cost in vision-language models by pruning, compressing or condensing visual tokens, with some papers on other efficiency and high-resolution adaptation methods for VLMs.
These papers benchmark and improve large audio-language models on acoustic perception, audio reasoning, bias, over-refusal and audio deepfake detection.
These papers reduce toxic generations, generate counterspeech and study how harmful content, fake news and poisoned corpora evade detectors, with a few loosely related robustness papers mixed in.
These papers evaluate and improve the spatial reasoning of vision-language models, including perspective taking, 3D visual grounding, geolocalization and remote sensing.
These papers benchmark and improve vision-language models on charts, diagrams, scientific figures and text-rich images, with a few studies on art, manga and specialized layouts.

topic: Synthetic Data Generation and Data Curation
about: These papers generate, select and audit synthetic training data for instruction tuning, pretraining and low-resource tasks, and design data mixtures and recipes for model adaptation.
These papers benchmark and defend multimodal and text-to-image models against unsafe generation, jailbreaks and culturally specific risks, using safety unlearning, detoxification and guard models.
These papers remove targeted knowledge from text and multimodal models while preserving utility, and test how robust the forgetting is to relearning and recovery attacks.

topic: Proactive Agents and Implicit User Intent
about: These papers benchmark and train agents that infer implicit user intent, elicit preferences and personalize multi-turn help in shopping, travel planning and assistant settings.

topic: Knowledge Editing and Lifelong Model Editing
about: These papers update or reverse specific facts and rules inside model parameters, covering batch, multi-hop, temporal and lifelong editing while preserving locality.
These papers compress, merge and quantize mixture-of-experts models and make MoE training and fine-tuning more efficient, alongside some work on the Muon optimizer and parallelism.
These papers recognize, explain and control emotion, sentiment and stance in text and conversation, and probe how models represent affect internally.
These papers improve how MoE models route tokens to experts, prune or reduce experts at test time, and fine-tune MoE models without breaking their routing structure.

These papers build and evaluate adaptive tutoring agents, student simulators and teacher-student dialogue corpora, alongside a smaller group of knowledge distillation papers pulled in by teacher-student wording.

topic: Theory of Mind and Social Intelligence
about: These papers benchmark theory-of-mind and social reasoning in text and multimodal models, from multi-party meetings and body language to deception and social deduction games.
These papers evaluate machine translation with LLM judges, error span detection, document context and human studies, including literary and culturally loaded translation.

topic: Meme Understanding and Harmful Meme Detection
about: These papers build multimodal models and multilingual benchmarks to interpret memes, humor and cultural references and to detect hateful or harmful memes.
These papers embed and detect watermarks in generated text and fingerprint models for copyright protection, balancing detectability, robustness to edits and text quality.

topic: GUI Agent Grounding and RL Training
about: These papers build benchmarks, GUI grounding methods, world models and reinforcement learning recipes for agents that operate desktop, mobile and browser interfaces.
These papers extract events, arguments and timelines from documents and connect language with time-series data for event detection, forecasting and temporal explanation.
These papers generate and evaluate radiology reports from chest X-rays and CT scans with medical vision-language models that stay grounded in images and clinical findings.
These papers build agentic systems and benchmarks for claim verification, regulatory and advertising compliance checking, fraud detection and evidence-grounded auditing in applied domains.
These papers analyze and redesign tokenizers, including byte-level, grapheme and morphology-aware subwords, and study their effect on multilingual and low-resource modeling.
